story: At 6:17 on a breezy, clear Saturday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at his workbench at home, laying out speaker wiring and light strips for Rosa while cornbread bakes nearby. Donna and Rosa are both heading out to Magnolia Loop, while Hal is already there, dutifully counting the flamingos he can see from the street and checking whether the hedge hides the rest. Everyone seems in good spirits as the warm November air settles over the neighborhood.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Lay out the speaker wiring and light strips to show Rosa the plan while the cornbread bakes
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count only the flamingos visible from the street and note whether the hedge screens the rest
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: Rosa is in my house walking around the cart while the cornbread bakes. I already invited her in and she's already committed me to Friday dinner, so no need to repeat that. The cart is my pride and joy, and the lights and speakers are still waiting on Architectural Review, so I can't install anything visible from the street yet. I can work at the workbench on the parts that don't show, like wiring the sound system, while chatting with her. That keeps me useful and busy without breaking L-01, and I'll keep the amplifier unplugged past quiet hours anyway.

parameters.content: Lay out the speaker wiring and light strips to show Rosa the plan while the cornbread bakes

donna.thought_process: I'm alone at the rec center, and I've already reserved the Tuesday slot and studied the ladder twice. No need to stare at the board a third time. Gary's still never played, so the better use of my evening is to get him ready: I should head home, freshen up, and be on time for Rosa's Friday-style dinner. Time to leave the courts and make an entrance with my deviled eggs.

parameters.content: Tuesday court time is booked and I've scoped the ladder. Heading out to freshen up before dinner.

hal.thought_process: I'm standing on Magnolia Loop with no one around, and the flamingo flock is right here. I've counted three times already and Rosa says the extras are behind the hedge, which is legal as long as they're not visible from the street. By-the-book means counting only what the street sees, and fair is fair. I'll do one honest count, note whether the hedge actually screens the rest, then let it go and save my appetite for Rosa's Friday dinner.

parameters.content: Count only the flamingos visible from the street and note whether the hedge screens the rest

rosa.thought_process: Gary just confirmed for Friday and even offered cornbread, so I got what I came for. Asking again would be silly. Donna and Hal are the other two seats I still need filled, and I've already saved Hal a chair and put coffee in ink. Best move is to head out to Magnolia Loop and track down Donna to lock in her answer, rather than lingering at Gary's.

parameters.content: Gary's in for Friday, so I'm heading out to find Donna and make sure she's at my table too.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
